To the extent that the amounts due to the Contractor exceed the amounts due to the Subcontractor the balance shall be recoverable from the Subcontractor as a debt. Any payment shall be dealt with as a final application for payment as set out in sub-clauses 11.12 to 11.16.

children.name: text
children: Following termination, all plant, equipment, goods and materials delivered to the Site by or for use by the Subcontractor shall be deemed to be the property of the Contractor notwithstanding that title thereto may not have passed to the Contractor. The Contractor may take possession of and use, or permit others to use, all such plant, equipment, goods and materials. The Subcontractor shall if required at any time by the Contractor forthwith remove from the Site all plant, equipment, goods and materials, and failing such removal by the Subcontractor within a reasonable time the Contractor may remove and sell the same and hold the proceeds after deduction of the cost of removal and sale to the account of the Subcontractor after deducting any monies that may be due from the Subcontractor to the Contractor.

children.name: text
children: For the purpose of completion of the Subcontract Works the Contractor shall have the free use of the Subcontractor’s equipment, materials and property on the Site without responsibility to the Subcontractor for fair wear and tear thereof and to any materials or fabricated work lying at the Subcontractor’s works or workshop which have been bought or fabricated for the purpose of this Subcontract. If requested the Subcontractor must assign to the Contractor within 14 days of the date of determination, without payment the benefit of any agreement for the supply of materials or goods and / or for the execution of any work for the purposes of this Subcontract to the extent that the same is assignable.

children.name: text
children: Upon determination of the Subcontractor’s employment the Subcontractor shall immediately deliver to the Contractor the possession of such part or parts of the Site possessed by the Subcontractor.

children.name: text
children: If there are step in or assignment rights and obligations within the Main Contract, then the Subcontractor is deemed to have accepted such and shall accept assignment or step in of the Employer / Funder and the like.

children.name: text
children: Notwithstanding any other provision of this Subcontract, Contractor may (without reason and at his sole discretion) terminate this Subcontract at any time by giving the Subcontractor a 3-day notice. If so terminated, the Contractor shall pay to the Subcontractor all payments properly due to the Subcontractor under this subcontract for Subcontract Works completed up to the date of such notice of termination and the Subcontractor shall not be entitled to any loss of profit or any other payment whatsoever in respect of the remaining works (and the Contractor may engage an alternative contractor to undertake the remaining works).

children.name: text
children: {b:Governing Law}

children.name: text
children: These terms and conditions shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of England and Wales.

children.name: text
children: {b:Adjudication}

children.name: text
children: A party to this Subcontract provided that the Subcontract is a ‘Construction Contract’ as defined by the Housing Grants, Construction and Regeneration Act 1996 as amended under Part 8 of the Local Democracy, Economic Development and Construction Act 2009 (“the Act”) has the right to refer a dispute arising therefrom to adjudication at any time.

children.name: text
children: Subject to the Act applying to the Subcontract, either party may give notice at any time of its intention to refer a dispute to adjudication. The notice of adjudication shall be accompanied by the referring party’s intended referral notice and all documents which are to be included in the referring party’s referral notice.

children.name: text
children: The referring party shall secure the appointment of the Adjudicator and serve the formal referral to him or her and the responding party not later than seven days from the date of the notice of adjudication. On receipt of the formal referral notice, the Adjudicator must inform every party to the dispute of the date it was received.

children.name: text
children: The Adjudicator shall reach a decision within 28 days after receipt of the referral or such longer period as is agreed by the parties after the dispute has been referred and shall set a timetable to enable this. In any event the responding party will be given 16 days to respond to the formal referral.

children.name: text
children: The Adjudicator may extend the period of 28 days by up to 14 days with the consent of the party by whom the dispute was referred, or such longer period as may be agreed by the parties.

children.name: text
children: The Adjudicator has a duty to act impartially.

children.name: text
children: The Adjudicator is able to take the initiative in ascertaining the facts and the law.

children.name: text
children: The decision of the Adjudicator shall be binding until the dispute is finally determined by an Arbitrator or in legal proceedings. The parties may agree to accept the decision of the Adjudicator as finally determining the dispute.

children.name: text
children: The Adjudicator is permitted to correct his or her decision so as to remove a clerical or typographical error arising by accident or omission. Any correction of a decision must be made within five days of the delivery of the decision to the parties.

children.name: text
children: The Adjudicator is not liable for anything done or omitted in the discharge or purported discharge of his or her functions as Adjudicator unless the act or omission is in bad faith, and any employee or agent of the Adjudicator is similarly protected from liability.

children.name: text
children: An Adjudicator shall be appointed within seven days of the notice of adjudication by the Royal Institution of Chartered Surveyors.

children.name: text
children: In case of any dispute arising under the Main Contract or between the Contractor and another Subcontractor or supplier connected with the Main Contract (referred to below as a Third Party Dispute) and the Contractor is of the opinion that the Third Party Dispute is substantially the same as or touches or concerns a dispute or potential dispute under the Subcontract then the Contractor may by notice in writing to the Subcontractor require that such dispute or potential dispute be referred to the same adjudicator appointed to decide the Third Party Dispute, who shall have the power to make such directions and all necessary awards and decisions in the same way as if the procedure in the High Court as to the joining of one or more defendants or joining co-defendants was available to the parties and to him.

children.name: text
children: In deciding a dispute between the Contractor and the Subcontractor under the Subcontract the Adjudicator shall be bound by his or her decisions as to fact in relation to such Third Party Dispute and the Subcontractor shall be bound by any decision or determination made in relation to the Third Party Dispute to the extent that and for so long as the decision or determination is binding on the parties to the Third Party Dispute.

children.name: text
children: If it is not possible for the same Adjudicator who has decided a Third Party Dispute to be appointed to decide a dispute between the Contractor and the Subcontractor a different Adjudicator may be appointed, but he shall be bound by the decisions of fact of the Adjudicator deciding the Third Party Dispute.

children.name: text
children: The Subcontractor shall afford at no cost to the Contractor such advice and assistance as the Contractor may reasonably require in respect of the conduct of any Third Party Dispute.

children.name: text
children: {b:Litigation}

children.name: text
children: Subject to 23 the English courts shall have jurisdiction over any dispute or difference between the Contractor and Subcontractor which arises out of or in connection with this Subcontract.

children.name: text
children: If any dispute arises in connection with the Main Contract and the Contractor is of the opinion that such dispute touches or concerns the Subcontract and the dispute is referred to an arbitrator or the court under the provisions of the Main Contract the Contractor may by notice in writing require at any time that the Subcontractor shall provide such information and attend such meetings in connection therewith as the Contractor may request. The Contractor may also by notice in writing require that any such dispute under the Subcontract be dealt with jointly with the dispute under the Main Contract and in like manner in which case any litigation proceedings currently taking place under the Subcontract shall terminate forthwith. In case of any such joint dispute the Subcontractor shall be bound in like manner as the Contractor by any award by an arbitrator or judgment of the court as the case may be.

children.name: text
children: {b:Notices}

children.name: text
children: All notices to be served by the Subcontractor on the Contractor and any other communications and any documents to be supplied shall be served by recorded delivery at the address to be specified by the Contractor or if none is specified at the address stated in the Order, or in the alternative shall be sent or transmitted by email to the email address stated in the Order. All notices communications and any documents to be served by the Contractor on the Subcontractor may be served in writing at the address stated on the Order or the Subcontract Pre-Order Meeting Minutes or may be sent or transmitted by email.

children.name: text
children: {b:Enforceability}

children.name: text
children: If any provision of the Subcontract is at any time found to be void or unenforceable such provision shall be deemed to be deleted from the Subcontract and the remaining provisions shall continue in full force and effect.

children.name: text
children: {b:Waiver}

children.name: text
children: Waiver by the Contractor of breach by the Subcontractor of any provision of the Subcontract shall not prevent the subsequent enforcement of that provision and shall not be deemed to be a waiver of that provision. The rights of the Contractor shall not be prejudiced or restricted by any indulgence or forbearance extended to the Subcontractor by the Contractor.

children.name: text
children: {b:Postponement and Suspension}

children.name: text
children: Where the Main Contract Works have been postponed or suspended by the Employer pursuant to an instruction given under the Main Contract or suspended by the Contractor exercising its rights under the Housing Grants, Construction and Regeneration Act 1996 the Contractor may direct that the Subcontract Works be postponed or suspended whilst postponement or suspension of the Main Contract Works is in operation. The Subcontractor shall not be entitled to any cost associated with any postponement and / or suspension.

children.name: text
children: If the Contractor fails to pay the Subcontractor the sum payable in accordance with any of the payment notices served under Clause 11 by the final date for payment and the failure continues for seven days after the Subcontractor has given written notice to the Contractor of its intention to suspend performance of any or all of the Subcontract Works stating the ground or grounds on which it is intended to suspend performance, the Subcontractor may suspend performance of any or all of its obligations under the Subcontract until payment is made in full.

children.name: text
children: Where the Subcontractor exercises its right under sub-clause 28.2, it shall be entitled to a reasonable amount in respect of costs and expenses reasonably incurred as a result of exercise of the right.

children.name: text
children: {b:Adjoining Highways and Control of Pollution}

children.name: text
children: The Subcontractor shall conduct all operations for the execution of the Subcontract Works so far as compliance with the requirements of the Subcontract permits, so as not to interfere unnecessarily or improperly with the convenience of the public, vehicular traffic or the access to or use or occupation of public or private roads and footpaths or to or from properties in the possession of the Contractor.

children.name: text
children: Notwithstanding the other provisions of the Subcontract, in carrying out the Subcontract Works the Subcontractor shall at all times comply with all statutes, treaties and conventions, directives, regulations and all codes of practice or conduct, circulars and guidance notes having legal or judicial import or effect whether of a criminal, civil or administrative nature, and the rules of common law, relating to or concerning pollution or contamination of the environment.

children.name: text
children: All reasonable precautions shall be taken to ensure the efficient protection of waterways against pollution, blockage etc. arising out of or by reason of the execution of the Subcontract Works.

children.name: text
children: In the event that any notice being served on the Subcontractor or any subcontractor of the Subcontractor under the Control of Pollution Act 1974, the Environmental Protection Act 1990 or any other Statutory Instrument, the Subcontractor shall immediately inform the Contractor of such notice and shall immediately comply with the instructions and directions issued by the Contractor in relation to such notice and / or restrictions of such notice.

children.name: text
children: In the event of any notice being served on either party, the Subcontractor shall provide all such assistance as the Contractor may require in relation thereto.

children.name: text
children: {b:Fossils, Antiquities, etc}

children.name: text
children: All fossils, antiquities or other objects of interest or value which may be found on the Site or when excavating on the Site during the progress of the Subcontract Works shall become the property of the Employer. Upon the discovery of the same the Subcontractor shall notify the Contractor and shall comply forthwith with any instruction issued by the Contractor.

Any loss or expense or any cost of delay caused by compliance with such instruction shall be reimbursed to the Subcontractor only to the extent that the Contractor has such entitlement under the Main Contract.

children.name: text
children: {b:Health and Safety}

children.name: text
children: The Subcontractor must supply the required information and adhere to the Construction Phase Plan as issued by the Principal Contractor appointed under the CDM Regulations. The said Construction Phase Plan may be subject to change.

children.name: text
children: The Subcontractor shall adhere to all the Contractor’s safety management systems and policies. Where a hazard is not rectified by the Subcontractor within specified times or in cases of imminent danger, the Contractor may use a third party to rectify the hazard and all costs incurred may be deducted from any monies due or to become due to the Subcontractor or shall be recoverable by the Contractor from the Subcontractor as a debt.

children.name: text
children: The Subcontractor shall comply with all the Health and Safety requirements of the Site including but not limited to:

children.name: text
children: The provisions of the Contractor’s Safety Policy.

children.name: text
children: A Risk Assessment and Method Statements for the Subcontract Works (risk assessments shall be provided for operations considered to be a hazard) before commencement of the Subcontract Works, to be provided by the Subcontractor.

children.name: text
children: COSHH assessments to be provided by the Subcontractor for all materials and processes used or adopted that are hazardous to health.

children.name: text
children: Valid certificates of training shall be provided by the Subcontractor in relation to all plant / equipment operators. All operatives and tradesmen shall be suitably experienced and competent to undertake their work and trained, with valid certificates of training where reasonably required.

children.name: text
children: Safety helmets, high visibility jackets and safety footwear shall be provided by the Subcontractor for its own operatives and tradesmen which must be worn at all times. The Subcontractor shall provide such other safety equipment and clothing as necessary for the hazardous condition or operation being undertaken as part of the Subcontract Works.

children.name: text
children: The Construction Phase Plan and Method Statements issued by the Principal Contractor, the Contractor or the Subcontractor.

children.name: text
children: The Contractor’s safety induction procedure which all operatives of the Subcontractor shall undergo prior to commencing work on the Site. They may be issued with an identification badge, which must be displayed at all times, if issued.

children.name: text
children: The instructions and recommendations of the Contractor’s Health and Safety advisors.

children.name: text
children: {b:Detailed Method Statement}

children.name: text
children: As and when required to do so, the Subcontractor shall submit to the Contractor’s Representative a detailed method statement, which shall amplify any previous method statement and detail the methodology on how the Subcontract Works are to be executed.

children.name: text
children: The said method statement shall include reference to such matters as location of access, direction of workflow, craneage and hoisting facilities, construction methods, materials handling, special design or specification constraints, provision of resources, temporary services and temporary work. All shall be described and programmed allowing time for comment by the Contractor’s Representative. Method Statements shall address health, safety, environmental and welfare issues.

children.name: text
children: {b:Environmental Conditions}

children.name: text
children: Where the Subcontract Works incorporate materials likely to be affected by environmental conditions, for example kiln-dried timber in floorings or joinery, ceiling tiles and decorating and the like, it shall be the responsibility of the Subcontractor to ensure that the environmental conditions are suitable in all respects before commencing the Subcontract Works. In each and every case where environmental conditions are not suitable, the Subcontractor shall notify the Contractor’s Representative in writing to that effect, giving the reasons.

children.name: text
children: {b:Setting Out}

children.name: text
children: The Contractor will provide a set of main reference points comprising base lines and datum levels and grid points at one level from which the Subcontractor shall set out its work and maintain such setting out. The Subcontractor shall also be responsible for checking any setting out carried out by other subcontractors, who may in any way affect the work to be carried out by the Subcontractor, and report to the Contractor or the Contractor’s Representative immediately upon any errors in setting out by other subcontractors becoming apparent. The Contractor will not be responsible for the checking of setting out of the Subcontract Works. The Subcontractor shall check the drawings and satisfy itself that all dimensions for setting out are correct.

children.name: text
children: {b:Subcontractor Provisions}

children.name: text
children: The Subcontractor shall provide everything which may be necessary to comply with all the current Codes of Practice, CDM Regulations and any other statutory obligations that relate to welfare matters.

children.name: text
children: {b:Builder’s Work Associated with the Subcontract Works}

children.name: text
children: Holes and other builder’s work for services of 50mm diameter or under, chases, recesses and the like shall be undertaken by the Subcontractor. All other builder’s work which the Subcontractor requires to be undertaken by the Contractor shall be clearly identified on drawings by the Subcontractor and submitted to the Contractor in adequate time to enable the Contractor to arrange for such work to be formed in the structure. The Subcontractor shall at its own cost undertake all builders work not so marked or identified, subject to first obtaining permission from the Contractor. The Subcontractor shall be responsible for all necessary sleeving and protection of services.

children.name: text
children: {b:Copyright, Royalties and Patent Rights}

children.name: text
children: The Subcontractor will be deemed to have allowed in the Subcontract Price or rates for all sums payable in respect of royalties, patented articles or other charges of whatever nature in relation to the Subcontract Works. Copyright of all designs developed or produced for the Subcontract Works shall become the property of the Contractor and a free, irrevocable, royalty-free and non-exclusive licence to use and reproduce such details is hereby granted to the Contractor for any purpose whatsoever. Such licence shall entitle the designs to be copied and used for any purpose whatsoever including (without limitation) the execution, completion, re-construction, repair, maintenance, modification, extension, mortgaging, advertisement, use, reinstatement, letting and sale of the Subcontract Works and the licence hereby granted shall also carry the right to grant sub-licences and shall be transferrable to third parties.

children.name: text
children: {b:Planning Approval Conditions}

children.name: text
children: The Subcontractor is hereby deemed to have full knowledge of the planning conditions applicable to the Main Contract and Subcontract (which may or may not be incorporated in the Subcontract) that are to be complied with at all times. The full planning approval document is available for inspection at the Contractor’s offices.

children.name: text
children: {b:Bribery Act}

children.name: text
children: The Subcontractor warrants that:

children.name: text
children: It will not engage in any activity, practice or conduct which would constitute an offence under Sections 1, 2 or 6 of the Bribery Act 2010;

children.name: text
children: It has and will maintain in place adequate procedures (adequate procedures as referred to in Section 7(2) of the Bribery Act 2010 and any guidance issued by the Secretary of State under Section 9 of the Bribery Act 2010), designed to prevent any associated person (associated person meaning the Subcontractor's persons and persons of any related company of the Subcontractor where related company means any Subsidiary Undertaking of the Subcontractor, any Parent Undertaking of the Subcontractor and any Subsidiary Undertaking of that Parent Undertaking where the expressions Parent Undertaking and Subsidiary Undertaking have the meaning given to them in Section 1162 of the Companies Act 2006 and undertaking has the meaning given to it in Section 1161 of that Act) from undertaking any conduct that would give rise to an offence under Section 7 of the Bribery Act 2010;

children.name: text
children: From time to time, at the reasonable request of the Contractor, it will confirm in writing that it has complied with its undertakings under this Clause 40 and will provide any information reasonably requested by the Contractor in support of such compliance; and

children.name: text
children: It will inform the Contractor, as soon as it becomes aware of same, of any potential or actual breach of this Clause 40.

children.name: text
children: {b:Modern Slavery Act}

children.name: text
children: The Contractor operates an anti-slavery and human trafficking policy throughout its business. The Subcontractor accepts that it will conform to that policy. The Subcontractor will not engage in any activity, practice or conduct which would constitute an offence under the Modern Slavery Act 2015. From time to time, at the reasonable request of the Contractor, the Subcontractor will confirm, in writing, that it has complied with its undertaking under this Clause and will provide any information reasonably requested by the Contractor in support of such compliance. The Subcontractor will inform the Contractor as soon as it becomes aware of any potential or actual, breach of this Clause.

children.name: text
children: {b:Confidentiality}

children.name: text
children: The Subcontractor acknowledges that information of a confidential nature relating to the Main Contract / Main Contract Works / business of the Contractor may be disclosed to it or otherwise come to its attention. The Subcontractor undertakes to hold such information in confidence and not, without the prior written consent of the Contractor, to disclose it to any third party nor to use it for any purpose other than in the performance of the Subcontract.

children.name: text
children: This obligation of confidentiality will not apply to information that is generally available to the public through no act or omission of the receiving party or becomes known to the receiving party through a third party with no obligation of confidentiality or is required to be disclosed by law, court order or request by any government or regulatory authority.

children.name: text
children: This undertaking will be binding for as long as such information retains commercial value.

children.name: text
children: No public announcement, press release, communication or circular (other than to the extent required by law or regulation) concerning the Subcontractor’s involvement with the Subcontract / Main Contract / Main Contract Works / the Site will be made or sent by the Subcontractor without the prior written consent of the Contractor. For the avoidance of doubt no photographs, digital images or the like are to be taken or obtained of any works within the demise of a Contractor’s project or associated areas.

children.name: text
children: The Subcontractor acknowledges that it will not use or permit to be used any drawings, diagrams, sketches, photographs or technical information supplied to it by the Contractor for any purpose other than the Subcontract and will return all such items to the Contractor on demand.

children.name: text
children: {b:Meetings & Supervision}

children.name: text
children: The Subcontractor or its duly appointed site supervisor shall attend regular progress meetings on Site with the Contractor, the Employer or its site representative such meetings to discuss (amongst other matters) progress of the Subcontract Works against the key dates and/or programme.

children.name: text
children: The Subcontractor is to provide a site foreman/supervisor to provide daily supervision for the duration of the Subcontract Works. The appointed supervisor/foreman must liaise with the Contractor regarding the day-to-day operations, attend and record site meetings, ensure sufficient labour is on site to meet the Subcontractor’s obligations and compliance with all Health and Safety requirements.

children.name: text
children: {b:Waste}

children.name: text
children: All waste materials arising from the Subcontractor's work are to be removed and the property or area to be swept clean at the end of each working day and ready for the following trades at the completion of each stage of the Subcontract Works. This is to be both inside and around the property or area and waste to be cleared to a point / rubbish skip designated by the Contractor.

children.name: text
children: The Contractor reserves the right to deduct from the Contractor's account to the Subcontractor the cost of removing from site any excessive waste generated by the Subcontractor along with the cost of any materials for work not carried out in accordance with the Subcontract Works.

children.name: text
children: Active waste shall at all times be kept separate from inactive waste, as defined within relevant landfill tax legislation.

children.name: text
children: All surplus materials must be moved to the next plot or returned to the store on completion of each operation and where supplied by the Subcontractor, removed from site by the Subcontractor at the conclusion of the Subcontract Works. Waste material must not be burnt on site.

children.name: text
children: {b:Survivorship}

children.name: text
children: Each indemnity and warranty in the Subcontract survives the expiry or termination of this Subcontract, as do the termination provisions and dispute provisions.

children.name: text
children: {b:Limitation Period}

children.name: text
children: It is agreed that irrespective of the manner in which this Subcontract is executed or made neither the Contractor nor the Subcontractor shall rely on any limitation defence that might otherwise be available in defence of proceedings commenced less than 12 years after the practical completion of the Main Contract Works under the Main Contract (or, if earlier, less than 12 years from the completion of the Subcontractor's works or termination of the Subcontractor's employment under this Subcontract).

children.name: text
children: The limitation period for commencing any action or proceedings under this Subcontract that arise (directly or indirectly) out of or relate to a breach of duty or liability under the Defective Premises Act 1972 or section 38 of the Building Act 1984 ({b:Special Limitation Period}) shall be the same as the applicable limitation period that would apply to an action or proceedings commenced under that legislation or under the Civil Liability (Contribution) Act 1978 in respect of any liability under that legislation, if later, (and not any shorter limitation period applicable to a claim for breach of contract under the Limitation Act 1980) and any such action or proceedings under this Subcontract may be commenced at any time prior to the expiry of the Special Limitation Period. The Subcontractor shall maintain professional indemnity insurance in accordance with (and subject to) this Subcontract in respect of any breach or liability referred to in this clause until the expiry of the Special Limitation Period.
